m: ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī, he said: We were at a funeral in al-Baqīʿ, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to us and sat, and we sat with him; he had a stick with which he was scratching the ground, and he raised his head to the sky and said: “There is no soul that has been born but that its entry [place] has been written.” The people said: “Messenger of God, should we not rely on our writing? For whoever is of the people of happiness will work for happiness, and whoever is of the people of wretchedness will work for wretchedness.” He said: “Rather, act, for everyone is eased: as for whoever is of the people of happiness, he is eased toward the work of happiness; and as for whoever is of the people of wretchedness, he is eased toward wretchedness.” Then he recited:

As for he who gives and fears God (5) And believes in the best [reward] (6) We will ease him toward ease (7) But as for he who withholds and considers himself free of need (8) And denies the best [reward] (9) We will ease him toward difficulty

c: Abū l-Sāʾib told us, he said: Abū Muʿāwiyah told us, from al-Aʿmash, from Saʿd b.
m: ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the like of it

c: Ibn al-Muthannā told us, he said: Muḥammad b. Jaʿfar told us, he said: Shuʿbah told us, from Manṣūr and al-Aʿmash,
m: that they heard Saʿd b. ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he was at a funeral, and took a stick and began scratching the ground, and said: “There is none but that his seat in the Fire or in Paradise has been written.” They said: “Messenger of God, should we not rely?” He said: “Act, for everyone is eased:

As for he who gives and fears God (5) And believes in the best [reward] (6) We will ease him toward ease (7) But as for he who withholds and considers himself free of need (8) And denies the best [reward] (9) We will ease him toward difficulty

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Manṣūr and al-Aʿmash, from Saʿd b.
m: ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him, he said: We were sitting with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he picked up something from the ground with his hand and said: “There is none of you but that his seat in Paradise and the Fire is known.” They said: “Prophet of God, should we not rely?” He said: “No; act, for everyone is eased for that for which he was created.” Then he recited:
As for he who gives and fears God
, the two verses. He said: Mihrān told us, from Abū Sinān, from ʿAbd al-Malik b. [Samurah Abū]

, from al-Nazzāl b. Sabrah, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no soul that has been born but that God has written upon it what it will meet.” And a Bedouin was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, seeking [instruction], and the Bedouin said: [“Then what makes me]

go off [to work] from such-and-such valley if the matter has already been settled?” So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, scratched at the ground, until the people thought that he wished he had not said anything of it, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Everyone is eased for that for which he was created; so whoever God wills good for, He eases him to the path of good, and whoever He wills evil for, He eases him to the path of evil.” Then I met ʿAmr b. Murrah and presented this ḥadīth to him, and he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and he added

As for he who gives and fears God (5) And believes in the best [reward] (6) We will ease him toward ease (7) But as for he who withholds and considers himself free of need (8) And denies the best [reward] (9) We will ease him toward difficulty

c: Yaʿqūb b. Ibrāhīm told me, he said: Hushaym told us, he said: Ḥuṣayn told us, from Saʿd b.
m: ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, he said: When this verse was revealed:
Indeed, all things We created with predestination

[al-Qamar: 49], a man said: “Messenger of God, then why act—is it in something we begin anew, or in something already finished with?” So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Act, for everyone is eased; We will ease him toward ease, and We will ease him toward difficulty”
b. ʿAbd al-Malik al-Ṭāʾī told me, he said:

c: Muḥammad b. ʿUbaydah told us, he said: al-Jarrāḥ told us, from Ibrāhīm b.
m: ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from al-Ḥajjāj b. Arṭāh, from Abū Isḥāq al-Hamdānī, from Sulaymān al-Aʿmash, who traced the ḥadīth back to ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib, may God be pleased with him, that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting one day with a stick in his hand with which he was scratching the ground, and he raised his head and said: “There is none of you, nor of the people, but that his seat in Paradise or the Fire is known.” We said: “Messenger of God, should we not put our trust [in that]?” He said to them: “Act, for everyone is eased for that for which he was created.” Then he said: “Have you not heard God say in His Book:

As for he who gives and fears God (5) And believes in the best [reward] (6) We will ease him toward ease (7) But as for he who withholds and considers himself free of need (8) And denies the best [reward] (9) We will ease him toward difficulty

c: Ibn al-Muthannā told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Mahdī told us, he said: Khālid b. ʿAbdallāh told us, from Dāwūd b.
m: Abī Hind, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās:
We will ease him toward difficulty

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: ʿAmr b. al-Ḥārith informed me, from Abū l-Zubayr, from Jābir b.
m: ʿAbdallāh, that he said: “Messenger of God, do we act
for a matter already finished with, or for a matter we begin anew?” So he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Every worker is eased for his work”

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Sufyān told us, from ʿAmr b.
m: Dīnār, from Ṭalq b. Ḥabīb, from Bushayr b. Kaʿb, he said: Two young lads asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: “Messenger of God, do we act (2) in what the pens have dried upon and the decrees have run by, or in something begun anew?” He said: “Rather, in what the pens have dried upon and the decrees have run by.” They said: “Then why act?” He said: “Act, for every worker is eased for his work for which he was created.” They said: “Then now we shall strive and act”

x: On the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

And what will his wealth avail him when he falls? (11) Indeed, upon Us is guidance (12) And indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first [life] (13) So I have warned you of a Fire blazing (14) None will [enter to] burn therein except the most wretched (15) Who denied and turned away (16) And the most devout will be kept away from it (17) [He] who gives his wealth [to be] purified (18)
. He, majestic is His praise, means by His saying
h
And what will his wealth avail him

: what thing will his wealth ward off, on the Day of Resurrection, from this one who was stingy with his wealth and considered himself free of need of his Lord, when he falls? Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the interpretation of His saying:
h
when he falls
; some of them said: its interpretation is: when he falls into Hell, that is, drops into it and plunges.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: al-Ashjaʿī told us, from Ibn Abī Khālid, from Abū Ṣāliḥ:
m: And what will his wealth avail him when he falls?
. He said: in Hell. Abū Kurayb said: al-Ashjaʿī heard that from Ismāʿīl

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah,
m: . He said: when he falls into the Fire

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: when he dies.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Wakīʿ told us, from Sufyān, from Layth, from Mujāhid:
m: And what will his wealth avail him when he falls?

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us,
m: both of them from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid

x: His saying:
h
when he falls
. He said: when he dies
n

c: [Abū Kurayb told us, he said: al-Ashjaʿī told us, from Sufyān, from Layth, from Mujāhid, he said:
m: . And the more correct of the two views is the view of those who said: its meaning is: when he falls into Hell; because that is the familiar meaning of “taraddā”; as for when the meaning of death is intended, one says: “radiya so-and-so,” and it is rarely said “taraddā.”

x: And His saying:
h
Indeed, upon Us is guidance
. The Exalted, whose mention is lofty, says: Indeed, it is upon Us to make clear the truth from falsehood, and obedience from disobedience.
The people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said about this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah,
m: . He says: Upon God is the clarification: the clarification of what He has made lawful and unlawful, and of obedience and disobedience to Him
used to interpret it to mean: that whoever takes the path of guidance, upon God is his way; and he says: it is like His saying:
And upon God is the direction of the [right] way
[al-Naḥl: 9]. And he says: its meaning is: whoever God wills is upon the direct way. And he said: it is said that its meaning is: upon Us is guidance and misguidance, as He said:
garments to protect you from the heat
[al-Naḥl: 81], while they protect from the heat and the cold.

x: And His saying:
h
And indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first [life]
And indeed, to Us belongs the dominion of what is in this world and the Hereafter; We give from them
n
to whomever We wish of Our creation, and We deprive of them whomever We will.
By that, majestic is His praise, He only means that He grants success in obedience to Him to whomever He loves of His creation, so He honours him with it in this world and prepares
n

for him honour and reward in the Hereafter; and He forsakes whomever He wills to forsake of His creation from obeying Him, so He humbles him through his disobedience in this world, and disgraces him with His punishment for it in the Hereafter. Then, majestic is His praise, He said:
h
So I have warned you of a Fire blazing

. The Exalted, whose mention is lofty, says: So I have warned you, people, of a Fire that blazes, and it is the Fire of Hell. He says: Beware of disobeying your Lord in this world and disbelieving in Him, lest you burn in it in the Hereafter. It was said
h
talaẓẓā

, when it is really “tatalaẓẓā.” And it is in the indicative position because it is an imperfect verb; and if it had been a perfect verb, it would have been said: “I have warned you of a fire that blazed (talaẓẓat).”
The people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said about this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us,
m: both of them from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, on the saying of God:

x: And His saying:
h
None will [enter to] burn therein except the most wretched
. Majestic is His praise, He says: None will enter it and burn in its blaze except the most wretched, [
h
Who denied and turned away
. He says]
n
: the one who denied the signs of his Lord and turned away from them and did not believe in them.
The people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said about this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Wakīʿ told us, he said: Hishām b. al-Ghāz told us, from Makḥūl, from Abū Hurayrah, he said:
m: “You will surely enter Paradise, except whoever refuses.” They said: “Abū Hurayrah, and who refuses to enter Paradise?” He said: So he recited:
. al-Ḥasan b. Nāṣiḥ told me, he said:

c: al-Ḥasan b. Ḥabīb and Muʿādh b. Muʿādh told us, both said: al-Ashʿath told us, from al-Ḥasan,
m: None will [enter to] burn therein except the most wretched
, and al-Ḥasan did not say it
—he said: the polytheist. One of the grammarians

used to say: He did not deny by an outright rejection, but fell short of what he was commanded of obedience, and so it was called denial (takdhīb), as you say: “So-and-so met the enemy and ‘denied,’” when he shrank back and turned around. And he mentioned that he heard some of the Arabs say: “Their fortune
has no ‘lie’ (makdhūbah),” meaning that when they meet [the enemy], they are true in fighting and do not turn back. He said: And likewise is the saying of God:
There is, at its occurrence, no denial [of it]

x: And His saying:
h
And the most devout will be kept away from it
. He says: and the God-fearing one will be guarded from the burning of the Fire that blazes. And “afʿal” was put in the place of “faʿīl,” as Ṭarafah said
n
: “Men wished that I would die; and if I die, that is a path in which I am not the only one.”
And His saying:
h
[He] who gives his wealth [to be] purified
. He says: the one who gives his wealth in this world in the rights of God which He made binding upon him,
h
to be purified
; he means: to purify himself of his sins by giving that.
On the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h
And no one has with him any favour to be rewarded (19) But only seeking the face of his Lord, the Most High (20) And he is going to be satisfied (21)
. One of the grammarians
n
used to direct the interpretation of that to: and no one of God's creation has, with this one who gives his wealth in the way of God to be purified,
h
any favour to be rewarded

, meaning: any benefaction for which he would repay him. He says: he does not spend what he spends of that, and does not give what he gives, as a requital to a person repaying him for a benefaction that person had done him, nor as repayment for a favour that has preceded from him to him with which he favoured him; rather he gives it in the rights of God seeking the face of God. He said: and
h
illā
in this place means “but.” And he said: it is permissible that the verb in the requital be future, so that its meaning would be: and he did not intend, by what he spent, any repayment from anyone.
And the place of the lām in “li-aḥad” would be in the pronoun that is put in the genitive by
h
ʿindahu

. So it is as if you said: “And he has no favour with anyone in what he spent, whose reward he seeks.” He said: And the Arabs sometimes put the particle in the wrong place when it is well known. And they cite as evidence for that the verse of al-Nābighah
n

: “And I feared, until my fear no longer exceeded that of a mountain goat at Dhū l-Maṭārah, sheltered (ʿāqil).” And the meaning is: until the fear of a mountain goat no longer exceeds my fear. And what the grammarian whose statement we have related said, claiming that it is permissible, is the correct one, which the reports from the people of interpretation have brought; and they said: it was revealed about Abū Bakr, for his freeing of those whom he freed [of slaves, seeking the face of God]
n
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah:
m: And no one has with him any favour to be rewarded (19) But only seeking the face of his Lord, the Most High (20) And he is going to be satisfied (21)
. He says: It is not for the recompense of people nor their repayment; his giving is only for God

c: Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm al-Anmāṭī told me, he said: Hārūn b. Maʿrūf told us, he said: Bishr b. al-Sarī told us, he said: Muṣʿab b. Thābit told us, from ʿĀmir b.
m: ʿAbdallāh, from his father, he said: This verse was revealed about Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq:
And no one has with him any favour to be rewarded (19) But only seeking the face of his Lord, the Most High (20) And he is going to be satisfied

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, [he said:
m: And no one has with him any favour to be rewarded
. He said: It was revealed about Abū Bakr, who freed people from whom he sought neither repayment nor thanks, six or seven; among them Bilāl and ʿĀmir b. Fuhayrah
. And according to this interpretation which we have mentioned from these, His saying
But only seeking the face of his Lord, the Most High
ought to be in the accusative, as an exception from the meaning of His saying:
And no one has with him any favour to be rewarded

; for the meaning of the discourse is: He who gives of his wealth does not give it seeking reward from anyone, but only seeking the face of his Lord. It is also permissible that its accusative be on the basis that what follows “illā” differs from what precedes it, as al-Nābighah said
: “…………… And there is no one in the abode except the tethering-places, which I scarcely make out ……………”

x: And His saying:
h
And he is going to be satisfied

. He says: And he is going to be satisfied, this one who gives his wealth in the rights of God, Mighty and Majestic, to be purified, with what God will reward him in the Hereafter as compensation for what he gave in this world in His way, when he meets his Lord. End of the commentary on Sūrat “Wa-l-layli idhā yaghshā”.

notes.en: Reported by Aḥmad, 6/449 (Maymaniyya edition); al-Bukhārī (3743, 6278); al-Nasāʾī in al-Sunan al-kubrā (8299, 11676); and Ibn Ḥibbān (6331), through Shuʿba. Abū ʿUbayd in Faḍāʾil al-Qurʾān (116), Aḥmad, 6/450–451, and al-Bukhārī (3742, 3761) reported it through Mughīra. Al-Suyūṭī attributes it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 6/358, to Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh; the Maḥmūdiyya manuscript, p. 453, adds Ibn al-Anbārī. Abū Ḥayyān says in al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ, 8/483: “The established reading in the regional codices and the mass-transmitted reading is ‘and by what He created, the male and the female.’ The hadith’s ‘by the male and the female’ is an isolated transmission that differs from the written text and is not considered Qurʾān.” Compare al-Qurṭubī, 20/81.
notes.ar: أخرجه أحمد 6/ 449 (الميمنية)، والبخارى (3743، 6278)، والنسائى في الكبرى (8299، 11676)، وابن حبان (6331) من طريق شعبة به، وأخرجه أبو عبيد في فضائل القرآن (116)، وأحمد 6/ 450، 451 (الميمنية)، والبخارى (3742، 3761) من طريق مغيرة به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 358 إلى سعيد بن منصور وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن مردويه، وزاد عزوه في المخطوطة المحمودية ص 453 إلى ابن الأنبارى. وقال أبو حيان في البحر المحيط 8/ 483: والثابت في مصاحف الأمصار والمتواتر {وَمَا خَلَقَ الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنْثَى} وما ثبت في الحديث من قراءة (والذكر والأنثى) نقل آحاد مخالف للسواد فلا يعد قرآنا. وينظر تفسير القرطبي 20/ 81.

notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 360 إلى المصنف وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر.

notes.en: Al-Bazzār (2209), al-Ṭabarānī in al-Kabīr (237, part of volume 13), Ibn ʿAdī in al-Kāmil, 1/2359, and Ibn ʿAsākir in his Tārīkh, 30/70–71, reported it through Bishr. Al-Suyūṭī attributes it to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh in al-Durr al-manthūr, 6/359.
notes.ar: أخرجه البزار (2209)، والطبراني في الكبير (237 - قطعة من الجزء 13)، وابن عدى في الكامل 1/ 2359، وابن عساكر في تاريخه 30/ 70، 71 من طريق بشر به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 359 إلى ابن المنذر ابن مردويه.

notes.en: Omitted from T2 and T3. S reads “he said: ‘He informed me from Saʿīd’”; M reads “he said: ‘Saʿīd informed me from Qatāda.’” Saʿīd is Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, as stated in the Maḥmūdiyya manuscript, p. 453, of al-Durr al-manthūr.
notes.ar: سقط من: ت 2، ت 3، وفى ص: "قال: أخبرني عن سعيد"، وفى م: "قال أخبرني سعيد عن قتادة"، وسعيد هو سعيد بن المسيب كما في المخطوطة المحمودية ص 453 من الدر المنثور.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributes it to al-Muṣannaf in al-Durr al-manthūr, 6/360.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 360 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: Its source references were given above, 7/483; both lines in full appeared at 1/183–184.
notes.ar: تقدم في 7/ 483، وتقدم البيتان بتمامها في 1/ 183، 184.
